audit.whatIsWrong: The difficulty story is built on Riposte 'parry-stunning' Rumble, which is stated in early, whys[1], wants.foe[0] and the full-layer cooldown block. It cannot happen.
audit.why: Riot's text: Riposte's stab 'slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' Rumble's entire kit contains no immobilise — Electro Harpoon and The Equalizer are slows, Scrap Shield is a shield plus move speed. So against Rumble specifically, Riposte can only ever slow. The lane is hard because of the damage parry and her vitals, not because of a stun.
audit.corrected: Riposte cannot stun you: it only stuns if it blocks an immobilise, and nothing in Rumble's kit is one. It parries the damage and slows — that is all.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says her Level 3 spike lets her 'parry your Electro-Harpoon, dash through your Flamespitter, and proc two vitals' with no cooldowns attached, and spikes[2] gives item advice with no Grievous Wounds timing.
audit.why: Riposte at rank 1 is 24s and only drops to 16s at rank 5, while Lunge is 13s at rank 1 falling to 6s. That gap is the whole spike: her dash comes back roughly twice per Riposte early, so the punish window is the ~20s after she parries, not a vague 'she takes over'. Her sustain (Duelist's Dance vital heals, Grand Challenge's area heal) is also never answered with an anti-heal timing.
audit.corrected: Riposte rank 1 is 24s; Lunge is 13s. Trade in the window after Riposte, and buy Grievous Wounds before her Grand Challenge matters.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interaction errors. (a) The 'parry-stun' claim (see point 2). (b) wants.you[1] tells you to keep Flamespitter channelling through her Q dash without noting that Riposte parries all incoming damage for its duration, so the Q ticks inside the parry are wasted. (c) Nothing records that Lunge applies on-hit effects, so her damage scales with attack speed and armour alone misreads the trade.
audit.why: Riposte parries all incoming damage for a short window. Flamespitter is a 3-second persistent cone, so the correct play is to hold the cone on her and let it keep burning after the parry expires rather than to start it into the parry. Lunge applying on-hit is in Riot's own description and is why her item spikes hit harder than a raw AD read suggests.
audit.corrected: Riposte parries all damage briefly and can only slow you; Flamespitter burns for 3s, so keep the cone on her and let it tick out the far side of the parry. Lunge applies on-hit, so her attack-speed items raise her damage, not just her AD.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block says 'Fiora Riposte: Parries autos/spells + stuns' — wrong effect, and no numbers.
audit.why: Corrected to the real behaviour and the real 24-to-16s range, with Lunge's 13-to-6s as the second entry so the player can count the two against each other.
audit.corrected: Riposte 24s to 16s, parries damage and slows; Lunge 13s to 6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing anywhere despite Fiora healing from both Duelist's Dance and Grand Challenge.
audit.why: _missing-interactions flags needs-antiheal for this exact pairing, and Riot's text confirms both heals. Extended trades and her R fight are decided by whether anti-heal is already down.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into the first-item spike text.

edits.after: At level 1 Fiora controls the pace — Lunge pokes in and out before your Flamespitter reaches Danger Zone, and it is only a 400-range step, so hug the wave and she has to commit. Play at max auto range and get one Q rotation off whenever she steps forward, but do not walk up to channel Flamespitter until Lunge is spent. At level 2 the threat escalates: Riposte parries all your damage for its window. It cannot stun you — the stun only happens when she blocks an immobilise and nothing in your kit is one — so the cost is the parried damage and a slow, not a lockdown. Throw one harpoon as a Riposte bait, then fire the second while her W is on its 24-second rank-1 cooldown. You still lose the sustained level-3 trade: her vitals out-DPS Danger Zone Flamespitter past two seconds.
edits.before: At level 1 Fiora controls the pace — her Q lets her poke in and out before your Flamespitter reaches Danger Zone, and she can dash away before you can punish. Play at max auto range and get one Q rotation off whenever she steps forward, but do not walk up to channel Flamespitter unless she has already used Lunge. At level 2 the threat escalates: she can Riposte your Electro-Harpoon on the spot, turning your main kite tool into her free-trade window. Try throwing one E first as a Riposte bait, then immediately fire the second shot when her W is down. You will not win a sustained trade at level 3 — her vitals plus true damage out-DPS your Danger Zone Flamespitter in any trade that lasts more than two seconds.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the roughest stretch. Riposte is down to roughly 18 seconds while Lunge has fallen to about 8, so her dash comes back twice per parry and she can proc vitals every engagement — even a clean Danger Zone trade costs you more HP than her. Flamespitter from the very edge of its range, W-shield the instant she dashes in, and disengage rather than channel into her follow-up. Note that Lunge applies on-hit, so her attack-speed buys raise her damage faster than her AD suggests. At level 6 the macro shifts your way: The Equalizer is a disengage and counter-engage she has no clean answer to, and threatening it over river or a dive forces her to respect your position. She still wins the straight duel, so spend it surviving her all-in or setting up your jungler, never on a solo kill attempt.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the roughest stretch. Fiora's Riposte cooldown drops to manageable and her Q cooldown is short enough to proc vitals every engagement, meaning even a well-managed Danger Zone trade will cost you more HP than her. Use Flamespitter from the very edge of its range and immediately W-shield when she dashes in, then disengage — do not commit to a full channel into her follow-up vitals. At level 6 the lane dynamic shifts slightly in your favor in a macro sense: Equalizer is a disengage and counter-engage tool that Fiora has no clean answer to in a skirmish, and threatening it over river or a tower dive forces her to respect your position. However, she still wins the straight 1v1 duel through this phase, so do not try to convert your Equalizer threat into a solo kill — use it to survive her all-in or to assist a jungler gank.

notes: Central correction: the page said Riposte 'parry-stuns' Rumble in four places. Riot's own text makes the stun conditional on blocking an immobilising effect, and Rumble has none — Electro Harpoon and The Equalizer are slows, Scrap Shield is a shield plus move speed. Against Rumble, Riposte only ever slows. Left alone as unverified: the existing claim that vitals deal percent-max-HP true damage is not in Riot's Data Dragon text for Duelist's Dance, so I neither amplified nor removed it. Kit-flag misfire noted again on rumble.json: Scrap Shield carries 'knockup' and 'terrain' flags that its description does not support.
